subject: Order Form Fee Exhibit — ceiling/floor language and discount ask
messages:
From: Jordan Weeks <j.weeks@atlascloud.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@atlascloud.com>
Cc: Samira Patel <s.patel@atlascloud.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fee exhibit redlines + floors/ceilings question

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached is our redlined version of Exhibit B (fee schedule) with two main asks:

- A floor that guarantees a minimum monthly spend while we ramp our usage.
- A ceiling on per-token pricing so our unit economics are protected in case usage spikes.

We're also asking for a 10% discount off list for committed spend of $480k/yr (equates to a $40k/mo baseline). If Redwood can agree to both the discount and the floor/ceiling language we can move to signature this month.

Can you confirm whether the "billable unit" definition in your template aligns with how you meter tokens for streaming vs sync calls? We had some internal questions on how KV cache hits are billed.

I've attached Atlas's redline (Atlas_OrderForm_ExhibitB_redlined.pdf). Please loop in legal if needed.

Best,
Jordan
Procurement
Atlas Cloud

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Weeks <j.weeks@atlascloud.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fee exhibit redlines + floors/ceilings question

Jordan — thanks for sending this over and for the clarity on Atlas's objectives. We can move quickly here. A few things up front:

1) Metering definition: our standard "Billable Unit" is per-1000 tokens processed (both input + output); KV cache hits reduce billed output tokens only when the cache returns the full block. I will have Marcus confirm precise wording for the Exhibit.

2) Discount/commit: we can consider a committed spend discount. Preliminary proposal from our side: 8% off list on committed monthly baseline (12-month term) with a monthly minimum that triggers a true-up if not met.

3) Floor vs minimum: we'd prefer to call it a "minimum monthly commitment" rather than an absolute "price floor" across all billing periods. That will let us keep predictable SLOs and avoid perpetual price locks.

I'll attach our latest pricing workbook with worked examples (pricing_workbook_v3.xlsx). Marcus — can you take point on the redline language for Exhibit B and propose clean replacement text? Karhtik, loop in if there are ramifications for tiered pricing.

Happy to set a 30-min call with Atlas procurement tomorrow to walk through the numbers. What time works for you?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Fee exhibit redlines — internal notes

Team — internal notes on Atlas redline. Key points to address before we push back:

- Nutshell ask from Atlas: 10% discount + explicit per-token ceiling + an explicit floor (they want a guaranteed minimum price protection).
- Sales recommendation: counter with 8% committed discount, minimum monthly commitment (dollar value) and per-token ceiling only for defined overage bands; avoid an irreversible "floor" that prevents future discounts.
- Commercial mechanics we need:
  - Define Billable Unit = "per 1,000 tokens" and call out KV-cache behavior.
  - Minimum monthly commitment = $40,000 (subject to final approval) with a monthly true-up.
  - Overage rate ceiling = $0.0012 per token for spikes beyond committed volume for first 90 days; then revert to standard overage rules.

Please see my talking points below that I plan to use on the call:
- We value Atlas and will provide a ramp-friendly commitment so their cost predictability improves during initial launch.
- We cannot commit to an indeterminate price floor that blocks runway for future promotional programs or platform pricing changes.

Marcus — legal sign-off needed on the suggested language around measurement window (monthly vs rolling 30-day) and annual true-up.

Thanks,
Neha
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fee exhibit redlines — legal input

Vanessa / Neha — reviewed Atlas's redline and Neha's notes. High-level legal guidance and proposed edits:

- Definitions: Replace vague terms with explicit definitions: "Billable Unit" = 1,000 tokens (input + output), "Measurement Window" = calendar month, "Committed Volume" = agreed monthly baseline in USD.
- Floor language: do NOT accept an open-ended "price floor". Instead we will accept a "Minimum Monthly Commitment" (MMC) expressed as a dollar amount with a monthly true-up to the MMC. This protects Redwood operationally while giving Atlas predictability.
- Ceiling language: acceptable as a short-term overage cap with explicit duration and a defined per-token ceiling for overage bands. Our proposed ceiling: $0.0012 per token for overage in months 1–3 post-go-live. After month 3, overage rates revert to the standard published overage schedule unless both parties agree otherwise.
- True-up & reconciliation: annual reconciliation with payment or credit to reconcile variance; for interim months do a monthly true-up (invoice/credit) to the MMC.
- Draft change: add a clause limiting the effect of Exhibit B to the Order Form term and specifying that future platform pricing changes (e.g., broad public pricing reductions) do not retroactively reduce Redwood's committed discounts.
- Risk/Termination: if Atlas fails to meet MMC for 3 consecutive months, Redwood may convert the account to pay-as-you-go or renegotiate committed terms.

I've prepared a marked-up Exhibit B (ExhibitB_clean_and_markup.pdf) with redline suggestions. Sales — confirm the dollar MMC you want to propose; I used Neha's $40,000 as the placeholder. Once you confirm, I'll produce a clean counter-exhibit for signature.

Marcus Lin
Legal Counsel — Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

Subject: Redwood counter: Exhibit B (fee schedule) — committed discount + mechanics

Jordan — thanks for your patience while we reviewed Atlas's redline. Attached is Redwood's counter-exhibit and a short explanation of the main commercial points. Summary below: 

- Committed discount: 8% off list pricing on committed monthly baseline (12-month term).
- Minimum Monthly Commitment (MMC): $40,000 per month. Monthly true-up to the MMC; annual reconciliation.
- Short-term overage ceiling: $0.0012 per token for overage in months 1–3 after go-live; thereafter overage follows published schedule.
- Metering: Billable Unit = 1,000 tokens (input + output). KV cache reductions apply to output tokens when cache returns entire token blocks; we added specific examples in the exhibit.
- Term & effect: Exhibit limited to the Order Form term and does not prevent Redwood from offering future public promotions.

Please review the attached clean counter (ExhibitB_clean_and_markup.pdf). If Atlas is comfortable with the MMC dollar amount and the 8% discount, we can prepare an amendment for signature.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow to finalize numbers? Options: 9:30am PT or 1:00pm PT.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
